title: Localization of a range quotient versus ModuleCat scalar extension
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, X,Y R-modules, f:X→Y linear, p a prime and A=R_p. Then LocalizedModule p.primeCompl (Y/range f) is A-linearly isomorphic to ((ModuleCat.extendScalars (algebraMap R A)).obj Y)/range((ModuleCat.extendScalars (algebraMap R A)).map f). This holds without finite generation or projectivity assumptions.

proof.text: Set S=p.primeCompl and A=R_p. For iX(x)=1⊗x and iY(y)=1⊗y, Mathlib IsLocalization.tensorProduct_isLocalizedModule exhibits both tensors as localizations. Their localized map induced by f agrees with f.baseChange A, by IsLocalizedModule.linearMap_ext on the generators.

LinearMap.localized'_range_eq_range_localizedMap identifies (range f).localized' A S iY with range(f.baseChange A). IsLocalizedModule.toLocalizedQuotient' shows that the quotient by this submodule is a localization of Y/range f.

Apply IsLocalizedModule.linearEquiv between the canonical localization of Y/range f and (range f).toLocalizedQuotient' A S iY. Extend this equivalence's scalars to A with LinearEquiv.extendScalarsOfIsLocalization, then transport along the range equality. Finally convert between the tensor-product module and the bundled ModuleCat.extendScalars object: both scalar actions are multiplication by algebraMap R A, by algebraMap_smul. These are genuine scalar-instance identifications, with no further mathematical assumption.

theorem residue_kernel_localized_cokernel
    (R : Type v) [CommRing R] (X Y : ModuleCat.{v} R) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (𝔭 : Ideal R) [𝔭.IsPrime] :
    Nonempty (LocalizedModule 𝔭.primeCompl (Y ⧸ LinearMap.range f.hom)
      ≃ₗ[Localization.AtPrime 𝔭]
        (((ModuleCat.extendScalars (algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime 𝔭))).obj Y)
          ⧸ LinearMap.range ((ModuleCat.extendScalars
            (algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime 𝔭))).map f).hom))
